sentenceSets.sentence: The lectures were designed to edify as well as inform, connecting abstract principles to the decisions students would eventually face.

answerChoices.reasoning: Instruction is the delivery of knowledge, which 'as well as inform' already covers, so the blank must name something the lectures added beyond the transfer of content.
Enlightening means clearing away ignorance, again a matter of understanding, while the sentence gestures toward the choices students will have to make and how they will make them.
'Improve' is too vague to stand against 'inform,' since better-informed students are improved; the contrast requires a bettering of character rather than of knowledge.
Inspiration works by kindling enthusiasm in the moment, but the aim described is to shape how students act when they later confront real decisions.
Entertainment would be an odd companion to informing in lectures explicitly built around principles and future conduct.
Persuasion aims at winning agreement to a particular position, yet no thesis is being argued for here.
Training builds practical skill through repetition, while the lectures work by linking abstract principles to eventual choices.
Assessment measures what students have learned and is not something a lecture is designed to do alongside informing them.
Confusing students would defeat the stated design of connecting principles to decisions.
No one designs lectures to bore, and boredom would undercut the informing the sentence credits them with.
Misleading contradicts a course built to prepare students for decisions they will face.

sentenceSets.sentence: The abbot chose readings meant to edify the novices, not to display the range of his own library.

answerChoices.reasoning: Uplifting concerns raising spirits and consoling, but the readings are selected for young men in formation, whose conduct and character the abbot is charged with forming.
Elevating suggests raising in rank or refinement, whereas the contrast with showing off his library points to the novices' moral schooling rather than their polish.
Reform presumes the novices have gone wrong and need correcting, but nothing suggests misconduct; they are simply being brought up in the life.
Ennobling implies conferring dignity or grandeur, a loftier effect than the steady instruction in right living that chosen readings provide.
Impressing the novices is closer to the display of his own learning that the sentence explicitly rejects.
Amusement is out of keeping with an abbot selecting readings for men in religious formation.
Testing would measure the novices rather than shape them, and no examination is mentioned.
Merely occupying their time would make the careful choice of readings pointless.
An abbot would not select readings to corrupt the novices in his charge.
Bewilderment is the opposite of what a deliberate choice of readings is meant to accomplish.
Intimidation belongs with the self-display the sentence sets aside, not with the purpose the abbot chose instead.

sentenceSets.sentence: Two hours of celebrity gossip had edified no one, as his sister pointed out over dinner.

answerChoices.reasoning: Enriching suggests adding to someone's inner resources broadly, including pleasure and imagination, while the sister's rebuke implies the evening left no one any better for it.
Education is the transmission of knowledge, and celebrity gossip does convey facts of a kind; the sister's complaint is that none of it did the listeners any good.
'Bettered' names improvement in the abstract without the note of moral or intellectual uplift that makes idle gossip the natural target of the remark.
Refining concerns polish and taste, but the sister's objection at the dinner table is to time spent with no worthwhile result rather than to coarse manners.
Gossip plainly informs its audience about something, so the claim that it did nothing for anyone must rest on a different kind of benefit.
Two hours of television may well have relaxed the household, which is why this cannot be the benefit the sister denies.
Distraction is exactly what gossip supplies, making it a poor candidate for something it failed to do.
Satisfaction concerns whether the viewers enjoyed themselves, not the improving effect the remark holds the program to.
Saying it coarsened no one would be faint praise and does not match a rebuke delivered over dinner.
Exhaustion is unrelated to the sister's complaint about how the evening was spent.
That the gossip offended no one would be a defense of it rather than the criticism the sentence conveys.
